title: Carrot, butter bean and orange soup

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a staple; vegetable stock counts as good stock, and tinned beans, yoghurt and seeds are all ordinary cupboard items.

supermarket.reason: Carrots, onion, garlic, butter beans, stock, an orange, yoghurt, pumpkin seeds and rosemary are everyday items at any Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: One heavy pan, a stick blender for soup and a grater for zest are all ordinary kit, and the technique is simple.

works.reason: 600g carrots, two tins of beans and a litre of stock blend to a good thick soup for four; 20 minutes softens sliced carrots, and the orange, rosemary and seasoning give it flavour.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is believable for chopping an onion, peeling and slicing 600g carrots, zesting an orange and toasting seeds, and the 5 plus 20 minutes in the steps matches the 25 minutes printed as cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, each name matches its id, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water-free stock.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming carrot soup with winter oranges suits a cold December lunch, and carrots are clearly the heart of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and plain British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Carrots, butter beans, yoghurt and seeds make a filling, proper lunch that a family would happily eat again.
